fixed_in_sweep: Root cause (engine.rs download_segment): the worker read (cur_pos, cur_end) once per iteration, then awaited the next chunk (and the rate-limiter wait). An idle worker's claim_or_split can split that segment mid-flight, shrinking its end. The worker then wrote/counted the chunk against the STALE (larger) end — bytes past the new end were counted twice (once in this segment's pos, once by the split-off segment that re-downloads them) — so sum(seg.pos - seg.start) exceeded total while the file itself stayed correct (same bytes at same offsets, which is why the hash matched). Fix: new pure helper writable_in_segment(pos, end, chunk_len); after the chunk fetch the live bounds are re-read and the chunk is clamped to the live remaining, acquire, then the bounds are re-read and clamped again via the helper before writing data[..n] at live_pos; plus a backstop clamping seg.pos to end + 1.

Safety nets: update_db clamps downloaded to total at persist; restore clamps downloaded_single (3 spots: restore_from_db + both sidecar restores in prepare); db.rs init_db runs a repair UPDATE downloads SET downloaded = total WHERE total IS NOT NULL AND downloaded > total (idempotent; unknown-total rows never clamped; fixes legacy inflated rows including completed ones, which restore never rebuilds).

Reproduction evidence: the new integration test FAILED 3/3 on unfixed code at 5 MiB, no rate limit (downloaded 5265404 exceeded total 5242880, excess 22524; 5254089, excess 11209; 5265404 again). With speed_limit_kbps = 500.0 it passed 5/5 pre-fix (shared limiter paces workers evenly, so remainders stay under 2x MIN_SPLIT when a worker goes idle and no split fires). The test is 64 MiB with 10 ms polls: a 5 MiB file flaked post-fix (kill point missed — download finished between polls, assert frozen < total) and a 16 MiB file flaked the same way; 64 MiB passed 3/3 post-fix (~33 s/run on this VM) and 1/1 pre-fix the race did not fire in that single sampled run (the race is timing-dependent; the deterministic unit test split_mid_chunk_never_double_counts is the proof it cannot reoccur).

Redirect finding: the update checker DOES follow HTTP redirects. check_manifest (update.rs) uses the shared reqwest client from engine.rs build_client, which sets only user_agent (and an optional proxy) — no redirect policy override, so reqwest's default applies (follow up to 10 redirects). Therefore the stable manifest URL is https://github.com/zulian026/zdm/releases/latest/download/version.json (GitHub 302-redirects it to the newest release's asset). The placeholder in index.html:314 uses it. Older-manifest behavior (from the update.rs test evaluate_newer_same_and_older): a manifest older than the running version evaluates to UpToDate, never an offer or an error.

Causes found by running linuxdeploy by hand: (1) FUSE is gone entirely (no /dev/fuse, no fusermount) — the linuxdeploy AppImage cannot mount; workaround APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 lets it extract-and-run.
